paper_title: Measuring the stability of fundamental constants with a network of clocks
coupling_convention: Fractional sensitivity/uncertainty on the fine-structure-constant variation, dα/α (dimensionless), exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 6b; NOT converted to the dilaton coupling d_e. X-axis converted from integration time τ[s] to mass via m[eV]=4.136e-15/τ.
notes: QSNET white paper presenting projected sensitivities (not measured limits) of a UK clock network to oscillating scalar dark matter coupled to the photon (1/Lambda_gamma, i.e. d_e^(1)) and electron (1/Lambda_e, d_me^(1)), shown as green curves in Figs. 6-7 spanning m_phi ~ 1e-24 to 1e-10 eV. The paper constrains both ScalarPhoton (alpha variation) and ScalarElectron (m_e variation) channels; ScalarPhoton chosen per pre-analysis hint and the primary Fig. 6a panel. However, no numerical sensitivity values are given in tables or text - the projections exist only as unreadable plot curves - so no data points could be extracted. If digitized later, note the y-axis is log10(GeV/Lambda_gamma), convertible to d_e via 1/Lambda_gamma = kappa*d_e with kappa = sqrt(4*pi*G_N). | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: The image labeled as the exclusion plot (fig_07) is actually an AC Stark shift plot; the plot matching the supplied axis calibration (x: 1-1e6 s, y: 1e-20 to 1e-15) is Fig. 6 panel (b) in fig_06.png, showing projected dα/α sensitivity vs integration time τ for clock pairs Yb+/Sr, Cf17+/Sr, Cf17+/Yb+, Cf15+/Cf17+. I traced the lower envelope (Cf15+/Cf17+, gold dotted), which follows ~4.5e-17·τ^(-1/2) with mild flattening beyond ~1e5 s. This is a projected sensitivity, not a measured exclusion; converting to d_e would require the DM field amplitude, so plotted dα/α values are emitted per the plotted-values contract. ScalarPhoton type chosen since panel (b) constrains α variation (panel (c) shows dμ/μ, which would be a different coupling). | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.41 snapped to identity)
